seen_animation: All 16 frames show the same black line drawing held almost still: a rounded square body that fills most of the frame, a two-turn spiral in its middle with a short flat stroke above the outer turn, and two short vertical strokes crossing the top edge near the right corner. Grey scenery stays fixed: a small circled minus sign at left, two bracket shapes on the right side, a small circled scribble below the bottom edge, and a vertical line plus a curved line at bottom right. Between frames only the inner spiral's ends and a few vertices shift by a pixel or two; nothing moves as a whole. It is a held shot.
seen_film: A static close-up of a camera front: a large circular lens with a knurled outer ring centered left of middle, a small bright central element, a screw at left, a vertical mechanism strip with bracket parts on the right edge, and a round knob below the lens. Across all 16 frames the camera does not move; only slight film grain, brightness flicker and sub-pixel weave change. It is a held shot.
named_subject: A camera (square body with a spiral lens and a viewfinder bump on top), drawn as the doodle.
evidence: Frames 1-16 of d.png are a static hold on the lens, and frames 1-16 of a.png are a matching static hold with no jumps. The spiral center sits at about the same place as the film's lens (left of center, upper-middle) in every frame, e.g. frames 1, 8, 16. The grey scenery matches film features at the same places: the circled minus at left matches the screw (frames 1-16), the right brackets match the side mechanism, the circled scribble below the body matches the bottom knob, and the bottom-right curve matches the lower housing edge. Frame-to-frame differences in a.png (inner spiral end in frames 3, 7, 11, 15 vs neighbours) are pixel-level, comparable to the film's grain flicker, and do not read as pops. This is judged from still frames only, not playback.

closes_when: The two vertical strokes at the top right are joined by a short horizontal top stroke inside the frame (by scaling or placing the body slightly lower), so the bump reads as the closed viewfinder box from c.png in all 16 frames.
